questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses that I have taken were my priority when choosing mobility. The campus at Alnarp was also very close to the UCPH therefore it was an easier destination when it came to moving etc.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Everything was well described and guided. Stress free experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Rooms in shared houses and dorms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The kitchen was very modern and well-equipped. There is a restaurant and cafe on campus both with reasonable prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It feels like living in a big family.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Everything was very easy. Most things such as enrollment to the first course were done after the arrival, in the first few days of the exchange.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Registration in the course; IT help with the account; library card etc. Everything without an issue.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress about it and ask for help if you are not sure about something.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very good level of education but not overwhelming. I learned a lot there.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Somewhat similar but definitely less stressful. There were multiple assignments throughout the course which contributed to the final grade along with the final exam. It was very different from UCPH where there was (usually) only one exam at the end of the course. The excursions were really interesting and overall great experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Sustainable forestry in southern Sweden

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer: Broadleaves - Forest dynamics, biodiversity and management for multiple use

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Broadleaves - Forest dynamics, biodiversity and management for multiple use. Very interesting course with great excursions. Great learning outcomes.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Internet was not provided at campus accommodation and had to be ordered additionally

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Most things were cheaper than expected as they are significantly cheaper than in Denmark. Alcoholic beverages are more expensive but personally that was not a problem for me.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Floorball is organized weekly on the campus. There are many social activities such as events in on-campus pub, organized by the student union. Since the campus is not located in the city, commuting (e.g. bus) is necessary to do some cultural activities in the city of Malmo or the town of Lund

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Events organized by the student union are a great way to socialize and get to know students from other courses.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Town of Lund is nearby and has many nice places to visit such as botanical garden. Sodarsen National Park is nearby and is a great place for hiking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in common dinners

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Meeting together for coffee is a very common custom

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Excursions are great experiences and a great way to learn so don't skip them.
Don't hesitate to ask for help as there are amazing resources dedicated to supporting you such as library.
Participate in social events as they are fun but also a great opportunity to get to know people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will meet a lot of students from different countries and backgrounds.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Passing the exams with the highest grade although learning happened throughout the course with minimal stress

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding the supervisors for my own thesis project was quite challenging and took some time but in the end, it was successful.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
